messages:
leah (customer-support): Heads-up — customer pasted a screenshot of their app logs in ticket #4721 and I can see a value that looks like one of our live API keys (starts with `rwd_live_7f4a...`). They attached the image.
leah (customer-support): screenshot (redacted):
```
INFO 2026-03-12 09:12:34 Request headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer rwd_live_7f4a...8b2d', path: '/v1/generate' }
```

sasha (sec_oncall): :eyes: thanks for flagging. can you paste ticket id + attach original image to this thread? do NOT copy the full token into chat.

leah (customer-support): ticket 4721 attached. redacted image uploaded to the incident folder: https://redwood.sup/attachments/4721/scrn1.png

sasha (sec_oncall): I'm going to treat this as potential exposure. immediate steps: 1) rotate/revoke the shown key 2) query access logs for last 30d looking for prefix `rwd_live_7f4a` 3) snapshot evidence and preserve audit log 4) check if customer used any private/dedicated resources (dedicated pools or private deployment).

jordan (eng-sre): running quick grep over proxy logs now: `grep -R "rwd_live_7f4a" /var/log/proxy/* | head -n 50` — returning 3 hits from 2026-03-11 22:03, 2026-03-12 01:14, 2026-03-12 09:11. IPs: 52.23.11.4, 18.194.2.7, 34.82.190.5. All requests were to `/v1/generate` with small prompt sizes, no usage of admin routes.

jordan (eng-sre): also checking API gateway metrics for spikes — none outside baseline.

sasha (sec_oncall): thanks. ben/infra — can you run `tokenctl revoke --prefix rwd_live_7f4a` in staging then prod revoke once audit snapshot is taken? Include request id for trace.

ben (infra): will do. snapshotting audit logs → `aws s3 cp s3://audit-exports/1720/export-20260312.json /tmp/4721-audit.json` then revoking now.

audit-bot: Audit event: token-revocation requested by sasha at 1719001252. action_id=rev-20260312-9a3b.

ben (infra): `tokenctl revoke --prefix rwd_live_7f4a --reason "support-screenshot-exposed"` -> action rev-20260312-9a3b queued. Revocation completed in prod at 1719001320.

sasha (sec_oncall): good. jordan — followups: run SIEM query for any successful calls post-revocation and check for unusual large bulk calls historically. Also pivot on the 3 IPs and enrich them in Threat Intel.

jordan (eng-sre): SIEM query: `index=api-requests token_prefix="rwd_live_7f4a" | stats count by src_ip, http_status, path` — results show 3 unique src_ip, status 200 for all, counts small (1,2,1). No request to admin endpoints. Will open TI enrichment ticket.

nina (product-security): we need to decide comms. Customer uploaded screenshot themselves; does the customer need immediate notification that their key was present in their ticket? leah, can CS confirm whether they redacted or pasted the screenshot intentionally?

leah (customer-support): CS reached out to customer for clarification — they said they pasted the screenshot to show an error to support and did not realize the header contained the key. They've rotated (client-side) their app keys locally but asked if we revoked the server-side key.

sasha (sec_oncall): we revoked our token. next: 1) ask CS to instruct the customer to rotate any keys on their side and invalidate cached tokens 2) check Dedicated/Private projects linked to that token (if any) — if yes, escalate to account team 3) prepare short comms: what happened, actions taken, recommended customer steps, ETA for post-incident report.

nina (product-security): also: post-incident items — add automated attachment-scrubbing to support UI (mask Authorization headers), add a quick-revoke button in CS console that calls tokenctl, and add an audit alert when support uploads images containing `rwd_live_` pattern.

sasha (sec_oncall): agree. creating follow-up GH task list now and assigning owners. immediate ticket created: GH#Redwood/sec-4721. tasks: (a) mask support attachments — @leah (b) CS notification template — @leah (c) console revoke button — @ben (d) SIEM enrichment & threat blocklist — @jordan (e) KMS check: verify whether any tokens are bound to customer-managed KMS keys — @nina.

ben (infra): quick note on KMS: if a key is HMAC-signed with a KMS-managed secret, rotating the KMS key can be an additional invalidation layer. in our current token system tokens are not tied to KMS keys — they are stored encrypted at rest with our KMS but the token verification uses internal signing key. we'll add a ticket to evaluate binding tokens to KMS key ids for future revocation improvements.

sasha (sec_oncall): good catch — add that as design doc item.

leah (customer-support): CS will send an initial message to the customer: short, factual, say we revoked the server token and recommend they rotate theirs and check for any unknown usage. will paste the template here for review.

sasha (sec_oncall): :thumbsup: thanks everyone. marking incident as contained. leaving post-incident follow-ups in GH#Redwood/sec-4721. we will produce a 72-hour interim update for the customer and a 7-day postmortem draft.

nina (product-security): also add audit rule: alert when support ticket upload contains strings matching `rwd_live_` or `rwd_test_` — low-noise threshold for now.

jordan (eng-sre): final note: all evidence preserved in `/incidents/4721/` and locked to sec+infra for 90 days.

leah (customer-support): uploaded customer-facing note to ticket and notified account owner. closing loop once CS confirms customer rotated keys.
